source: Belfield, S. and Brown, C. (2010). Guidebook on Upland Crops in Cambodia: Corn (សៀវភៅណែនាំ ស្តីពីដំណាំតំបន់ខ្ពង់រាបនៅក្នុងប្រទេសកម្ពុជា៖ ដំណាំពោត). ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. text:
Common fertilizer products sold in Cambodia and their nutrient composition, as summarised in this source:

- Urea: 46% nitrogen (N), 0% phosphorus, 0% potassium, 0% sulfur.
- DAP (di-ammonium phosphate): 18% N, 20% phosphorus (P), 0% potassium, 1.6% sulfur (S) -- the sulfur content is noted as being present in some DAP but may not always be included, depending on the specific product.
- NPK 15-15-15: 15% N, 15% P, 15% potassium (K), 0% sulfur.
- KCl (muriate of potash): 0% N, 0% P, 50% K, 0% sulfur.

DAP is the most commonly used phosphorus source, typically applied at planting; KCl (muriate of potash) is the most common potassium source. See the nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium management topics for specific application rates and timing.
